newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks finish mixed, major players keep off.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks finish mixed, major players keep off.

text.p: Indian share prices closed mixed on Friday with major market participants staying out and speculators driving the trade, brokers said.
On the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), activity was focussed on frontline stocks which showed little change from their previous closing rates in lacklustre volumes.
"Trading volumes were mostly speculative in nature with not much of investment buying noticed," said the chief dealer of a brokerage firm. "There was no definite trend in share prices."
The benchmark 30-share BSE index closed at 3,250.66 points, down 0.28 points.

Traders said the last day of trade at the Bombay Stock Exchange on Friday forced speculators to cover short-sold positions in active stocks. Dull volumes and little movement in prices of blue-chips characterised trading activity.
After rising about 212 points or over 6.5 percent in the first two day's of trade earlier this week, the index fell 90.92 points on Thursday, snapping the market's winning streak.

The National index closed 2.33 percent down at 1,445.53 points. "The market witnessed a marginal recovery and prices of pivotals gained," the NSE said. The NSE-50 Index closed at 936.95, gaining 4.18 points over the previous close.
The net traded value on the NSE was 11.72 billion rupees, net traded quantity was 60.4 million shares, NSE said.
The top five gainers on the NSE were Somkan Marine Foods, Nihon Nirman, Compact Disc, KHSL Industries and Soma Textiles.
Top firms including Bajaj Auto, Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company and Tata Iron & Steel Company will announce their six month results for 1996/97 (April-March) next week.
Analysts said the market would be looking to seek direction after the results of these major firms are announced.
SBI was up 4.25 rupees to 230.0, Reliance 2.0 to 211.0, TISCO 3.75 to 189.75 and TELCO 0.50 to 425.0. ACC lost 20.0 to 1,545.0, Hind Lever 4.0 6 to 814.0 and M&M 5.50 to 322.25.
Institutional purchases and mutual fund buying pushed up Delhi Stock Exchange index close 4.26 points higher at 737.97.
ACC, Reliance Industries, State Bank of India and TISCO were the gainers in Delhi.
